findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed a soil accumulation on the baffles of the ice machine. Per the follow up the ice machine was supposed to be cleaned however inspector observed the ice machine to be in the same state as the previous inspection.  PIC was made aware. PIC ensured inspectors that the ice machine will be cleaned.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: (2nd REPEAT) Employees were observed donning gloves without handwashing. Education was carried out and the behavior was corrected. Ensure that employees are knowledgeable to always wash their hands before donning gloves including in between tasks.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed the cook in the kitchen using their bare hands to place toast on to plates to serve. PIC was made aware and the pieces of toast were voluntarily discarded. Ensure that contamination from hands is prevented by using a barrier when handling ready to eat foods.
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Upon arrival the inspectors observed a soiled fork in the handwashing sink. PIC was made aware and the fork was removed to correct the violation. Ensure that handwashing sinks are used for handwashing only.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
Inspectors observed the following:

Soil accumulation was observed on the baffles of the ice machine. PIC was made aware. PIC ensured inspectors that the ice machine will be cleaned. 

(REPEAT) Inspector observed the soda nozzles at the servers station to have a build-up of soils on them. CORRECTED Discussed with PIC, and PIC removed the nozzles to clean them immediately. 
Ensure that food contact surfaces are monitored, cleaned, and sanitized at a regular frequency.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: (2nd REPEAT) Inspector observed several drain flies in the utility closet and the first and second aisle in the dry storage. Discussed with PIC. Ensure the flies are dealt with using authorized pest control methods. Zappers and fly strips may be hung, but they must not be hung over food. Ensure that pest activities is reduced within the facility.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed a large gap on the bottom of the back door of the dry storage area. PIC was informed. Ensure the gap is sealed by next routine inspection to prevent the entry of pests.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
findings.comment: There was a  wet wiping cloths just laying on the back counter top in the prep area. PIC was made aware. Education was carried out. The wet cloth was taken to get laundered. Ensure that wiping cloth is kept in a sanitizer solution in between use.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: (REPEAT X 3) Inspector observed there to be a build-up of oils and food debris behind the grill and griddle on the line. Ensure that these areas are cleaned regularly enough to mitigate the build-up of oils and food debris. Correct by next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed a glass of water without a lid and straw on the back counter in the prep area. PIC was made aware and the cup was removed to correct the violation. Ensure that employee drinks are covered with a lid and straw as well as stored in an area that protected from contamination.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Four packs of raw breakfast sausages were observed being stored above lettuce and boiled potatoes. Education was carried out. The sausages were removed and stored correctly. Ensure that staff are reminded to properly store food items in order to avoid cross-contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.comment: The gravy and cheese sauce were observed not holding the proper temperatures. The cheese sauce was temping at 116 and the gravy at 109. Discussed with PIC. PIC told inspector that one of the wells was not working. The gravy in that well was discarded. The cheese sauce was taken to be reheated. Inspector later reexamined the temperature of the cheese sauce and it was observed at 154F. Ensure that hot holding temperatures are monitored at a regular frequency to avoid spoilage.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed there to be several areas in the kitchen in need of a general cleaning. Areas include:

1) The kitchen floors, especially behind and around equipment.
2) Walls behind prep areas, they are especially susceptible to soil build-up.
3) Dry storage rack in kitchen has lots of flour and other debris on it.
4) The dry storage room has some items spilling on to the floor, as well as some flour and other food debris. 
5) Under the crock pot that is currently not in use.

Ensure these areas are cleaned regularly to prevent soil build-up.

Also, observed the dish machine to be soiled with dead roaches and food crumbs. Clean the dish machine.

findings.comment:
Inspector observed dish machine to not be dispensing sanitizer. PIC primed dish machine, at which point it was dispensing 100ppm of chlorine sanitizer. After one wash, it had halved in concentration. After a second wash, chlorine was no longer present. PIC informed inspector that they are going to call and have machine serviced. Inspector will return 12/20/2024 to evaluate dish machine again. Owner stated that MJ Kellner was en route during the inspection. The facility has access to a triple sink that will be used in the interim.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple life-stages of roaches in establishment. Roaches were observed both roaming freely and also on sticky traps in large concentrations. This is indicative of a reproducing population on the premises. PIC stated that pest control is coming twice a month, yet the problem persists. The facility is not cleaning sufficiently resulting in accumulating grease and food crumbs throughout the facility (see violation #s 16, 49, and 55). Despite coming every two weeks, Bacon’s Pest Control will not be able to properly combat the problem if cleaning is not appropriate. The facility is about to experience another closure due to pests should there not be a concerted cleaning effort. The facility should close for a detail cleaning and then maintain clean before having PCO service again. There is enough food present roaches have abundant food sources. The follow-up is being scheduled for January 13 in-order to allow time for detail cleaning.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Observed date marking to be missing on multiple TCS food being kept longer than 24 hours. Discussed with PIC, date marking stickers were prepared and placed on foods. Ensure any TCS food kept longer than 24 hours is properly date marked. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).
